items.text: plot draw a graph to represent information

items.label: text
items.text: plunger a part of a syringe that moves in and out

items.label: text
items.text: polar a polar covalent bond is one in which electrons are not equally distributed between the two atoms

items.label: text
items.text: polymer a large molecule made when many small molecules (monomers) join together. It consists of many repeat units

items.label: text
items.text: polymerisation joining up of lots of small molecules (monomers) to make one big molecule (polymer)

items.label: text
items.text: pop a sudden short sound, often loud

items.label: text
items.text: position of equilibrium a reference to the proportion of the various things in an equilibrium mixture. If the position of equilibrium of a reaction lies towards to the right, the equilibrium mixture contains a higher proportion of products than reactants

items.label: text
items.text: pour make something flow out of a container by holding it at an angle

items.label: text
items.text: precipitate a fine solid that is formed by a chemical reaction involving liquids or gases

items.label: text
items.text: precipitation reaction a chemical reaction in which a fine solid is formed from liquids or gases

items.label: text
items.text: pressure the force acting on something per unit area. Pressure has the Sl unit of Pa (N/m²) and is caused by molecules hitting the walls of their container

items.label: text
items.text: proton a subatomic particle in the nucleus of an atom. It has a relative mass of 1 and a relative charge of 1+. Number of protons in an atom = atomic number

items.label: text
items.text: proton number same as atomic number

items.label: text
items.text: quicklime calcium oxide

items.label: text
items.text: radioactive having an unstable nucleus that will emit particles and waves to achieve a more stable nucleus

items.label: text
items.text: range a number of things that are all of the same general type, or the extent of a variable or series

items.label: text
items.text: rate the speed at which the amount of reactants decreases or the amount of products increases. It is measured as a change in the concentration (or amount) of reactants or products per unit time

items.label: text
items.text: reactivity series a list of elements (mainly metals) in order of decreasing reactivity

items.label: text
items.text: redox reduction and oxidation. A redox reaction involves both reduction and oxidation occurring together reducing agentsomething that reduces something else by giving electrons to it. A reducing agent is oxidised in a chemical reaction reduction loss of oxygen or gain of electrons refinery gases a mixture ofmethane, ethane, propane and butane. This mixture is commonly used as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) for domestic heating and cooking relative atomic mass the weighted average mass of the isotopes of the element, relative to the mass of 1/12th of a 12C atom relative formula mass the weighted average mass of a formula unit of a compound, relative to the mass of 1/12th of a 12C atom. It is sometimes called relative molecular mass, when it refers to covalent molecules relative isotopic massthemass of one particular isotope of the element, relative to the mass of 1/12th of a 12C atom repeat unitthe basic unit which repeats itself in a chain to form a polymer residue the solid left on the filter paper during filtration reverse reaction fromproducts to reactants (the rightto-left reaction)

items.label: text
items.text: reversible a reversible reaction is one that can go both ways, in other words, reactants react to form products and products can react to form reactants

items.label: text
items.text: R value the retardation factor, which is calculated as the distance moved by a spot (from the pencil line) divided by the distance moved by the solvent front (from the pencil line) on a chromatogram

items.label: text
items.text: rust the corrosion of iron in the presence of water and oxygen. The rust formed has the formula Fe2O3-xH2O, where x is a variable number, and can be called hydrated iron(III) oxide

items.label: text
items.text: sacrificial protection a method of preventing rusting by attaching a block of a more reactive metal to iron. The more reactive metals undergo oxidation in preference to the iron

items.label: text
items.text: salt a compound formed when a hydrogen is replaced by a metal or ammonium in an acid

items.label: text
items.text: saturated compound a compound containing only carbon-carbon single bonds with no carbon-carbon double or triple bonds

items.label: text
items.text: saturated solution a solution that contains as much dissolved solid as possible at a particular temperature
